 Rodrigo Muniz (right) is congratulated as Fulham take the lead at the Etihad. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA View image in fullscreen Rodrigo Muniz (right) is congratulated as Fulham take the lead at the Etihad. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Barry Glendenning Sat 21 Nov 2026 08.30 EST First published on Sat 21 Nov 2026 06.25 EST Share Key events 11m ago Manchester City 0-1 Fulham 
 45m ago GOAL! Manchester City 0-1 Fulham (Muniz 16) 
 1h ago Manchester CIty v Fulham is go ... 
 2h ago Manchester City v Fulham line-ups 
 2h ago Premier League: Manchester City v Fulham 
 4m ago 08.29 EST That disallowed Haaland goal: According to Ifab Law 12 “A goalkeeper is considered to be in control of the ball with their hand(s)/arm(s) when: the ball is between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface (eg ground, own body.”
 Going by that and having seen several more replays, it’s this humble minute-by-minute reporter’s view that the decision to disallow Haaland’s effort was the correct one.
 Share Updated at  08.30 EST 8m ago 08.24 EST Some correspondence: “What a strange, but entertaining half,” writes Justin Kavanagh. “Haaland looks like he couldn’t buy a goal, while David Affengruber seems to be channeling his inner Bobby Moore in a Fulham shirt.”
 “Ref here,” writes Paul Pooley. “Two hands is not the standard. Control can be as little as one finger on the ball against the turf. The question is did Haaland play the ball when Leno had a hand on the ball against the ground.”
 “No doubt there’ll be focus on the disallowed goal (can see why not given, even if soft),” writes Shaun T. “But I also think it should be highlighted what an awful miss/bad connection from Haaland that was too. He had time to watch that Ndiaye cross right onto his foot and should really be burying that.”
 Share 11m ago 08.21 EST Manchester City 0-1 Fulham
 Half-time: Fulham lead courtesy of an excellent striked from Rodrigo Muniz, while City will feel they were unfairly denied an equaliser when Erling Haaland was penalised for bundling the ball over the line when Bernd Leno was in full control of it. It looked a harsh decision but the real story of this first half has revolved around how sluggish and off the pace City’s players have looked. Enzo Maresca has a big job on his hands if his side are to avoid their fourth consecutive top flight defeat.
 Share 15m ago 08.18 EST 45+2 min: The half ends with Bernd Leno saving easily from a half-hearted Jeremy Doku shot.
 Share 15m ago 08.17 EST 45+1 min: David Affengruber has been outstanding at the back for Fulham today and excels again here. He stands his ground to take the ball off Iliman Ndiaye’s toe after the City winger had jinked his way into the Fulham box and was about to unleash a shot.
 Share 17m ago 08.16 EST 44 min: With his arm in the air appealing for a free-kick that isn’t awarded, Nico O’Reilly completely switches off and allows Oscar Bobb to nip in behind him and shoot on goal from about eight yards out. Donnarumma denies the Fulham winger with an excellent save. That’s shocking – City are a mess!
 Share 19m ago 08.13 EST 41 min: Elliot Anderson advances towards the Fulham penalty area after winning the ball and plays a weighted pass to Nico O’Reilly. He eschews a shooting opportunity in favour of teeing up Haaland with a sideways pass but the Norwegian’s poor effort is way off-target. It takes a deflection to go out for a corner, from which nothing comes.
 Share 22m ago 08.11 EST 40 min: The City fans aren’t happy with their team’s extremely lacklustre performance and are jerring and whistling their players for not pressing Bernd Leno and assorted Fulham defenders as they pass the ball around the back.
 Share 23m ago 08.10 EST 37 min: City win a corner after good work from Jeremy Doku, who appeared to be fouled on the edge of the City area by Kenny Tete. From that set-piece, City win another. Phil Foden plays it short to Anderson near the edge of the penalty area but Fulham force their hosts backwards.
 Share 25m ago 08.07 EST 35 min: Erling Haaland sends a wild shot high and wide after running on to a beautifully weighted pass through the Fulham penalty area from Phil Foden.
 Share 27m ago 08.05 EST 33 min: Bernd Leno stands over the stationary ball after receiving a backpass and makes no effort to do anything with it, letting the clock tick down. Various City fans impatiently roar at Erling Haaland to press the German goalkeeper and force him into some sort of action.
 Share Updated at  08.06 EST 30m ago 08.03 EST 32 min: A Shea Charles cross from the right aimed towards Rodrigo Muniz is headed clear. Manchester City are looking very flat and vulnerable this afternoon.
 View image in fullscreen Sit down you’re rocking the boat… Photograph: MCFC/Getty Images Share Updated at  08.10 EST 31m ago 08.01 EST 30 min: A stray pass from Affengruber to Bassey is pounced on by Iliman Ndiaye near the halway line but a promising attack breaks down when Kenny Tete wins it back in the Fulham right-back area.
 Share 33m ago 07.59 EST 28 min: I think Fulham might have got away with one there, because Leno did have two hands on the ball at one point, he didn’t appear to have it under anything resembling control as Haaland bore down on him to force it over the line with his second attempt.
 Share 35m ago 07.58 EST 24 min: Iliman Ndiaye floats a superb cross into the Fulham penalty area from the right. Haaland connects with a thigh from about three yards out. Bernd Leno stops the ball only for the City striker to force the ball over the line with his follow-up. Haaland thinks he’s scored but his “goal” is disallowed because Leno is adjudged to have had two hands on the ball. Did he? I’m not so sure.
 View image in fullscreen Two hands? Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP Share Updated at  08.04 EST 38m ago 07.54 EST 23 min: Jeremy Doku tries to pick out Iliman Ndiaye with a lofted diagonal pass to the byline but overhits his delivery. The Senegal international is unable to prevent the ball from going out of play.
 Share 40m ago 07.53 EST 22 min: Calvin Bassey gets booked for a foul on Phil Foden, who is marking the ninth anniversary of his Manchester City debut. Nine years, eh? Where does the time go?
 Share 41m ago 07.52 EST 20 min: It was, to be fair, a fine finish from Muniz, who took a touch and curled an unstoppable effort past Donnarumma after Elliot Anderson and Ruben Dias had ushered Oscar Bobb through to provide the assist.
 Share 43m ago 07.50 EST 18 min: City have received a lot of criticism for conceding cheap goals in recent games and that’s another one to add to the list. A back-to-front effort in which both Bobb and Muniz went completely unchallenged as the visitors carved their way through the City bystanders.
 Share 45m ago 07.48 EST GOAL! Manchester City 0-1 Fulham (Muniz 16)
 And there it is! From a throw-in deep inside their own half, Fulham advance down the right with Oscar Bobb on the ball. He cuts inside and plays the ball to Rodrigo Muniz, who opens his body and curls a shot high past Gianluigi Donnarumma.
 View image in fullscreen Rodrigo Muniz strikes to give Fulham the lead! Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA View image in fullscreen Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at  07.53 EST 46m ago 07.46 EST 15 min: It’s been a fairly sedate return for the Premier League thus far and the crowd at the Etihad Stadium seem half-asleep. This game needs a goal to perk them up.
 Share 47m ago 07.45 EST 14 min: On his return to his former club, Oscar Bobb fouls Nico O’Reilly halfway inside the Fulham half to concede a cheap free-kick.
 Share 49m ago 07.44 EST 12 min: Ayyoub Bouaddi wins the ball from Kenny Tete in midfield and sends Manchester City on their weay upfield. Fulham don’t take long to win the ball back as Jeremy Doku runs into traffic.
 Share 51m ago 07.42 EST 11 min: Fulham corner. Alex Iwobi plays it long beyond the far post towards Kenny Tete but Jeremy Doku is able to hook the ball clear.
 Share 52m ago 07.41 EST 10 min: A Nico O’Reilly shot is put behind for a corner by Affengruber, but nothing comes of the set-piece, which Fulham clear.
 Share 53m ago 07.40 EST 8 min: Jeremy Doku sends a cross to the far post, Erling Haaland heads the ball back across the face of goal and David Affengruber leaps highest to nod the ball away from danger. Moments previously, the Fulham defender had done well to block an Erling Haaland shot.
 Share 55m ago 07.38 EST 6 min: Manchester City play the ball hither and yon inside their defensive third, trying to play their way through the Fulham press. There’s an early yellow card for Iwobi, who is booked for holding Elliot Anderson as the City midfielder tried to spin him.
 Share 1h ago 07.35 EST 4 min: A Sander Berge cross from the byline is put out for as Fulham corner following a mix-up between Iliman Ndiaye and Ruben Dias. Donnarumma fields the inswinger from Alex Iwobi.
 Share 1h ago 07.34 EST 3 min: Now Bernd Leno gets on the ball, lumping it long towards Rodrigo Muniz. The ball’s played wide to Kenny Tete, whose cross from the right is plucked from the air by Donnarumma.
 View image in fullscreen Kenny Tete burts through Jeremy Doku and Phil Foden. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  07.40 EST 1h ago 07.33 EST 2 min: A goalkeeper under a little bit of pressure after some recent ricks, Gianluigi Donnarumma gets a couple of early touches, fielding two back-passes with a minimum of fuss.
 Share 1h ago 07.31 EST Manchester CIty v Fulham is go ...
 1 min: Fulham get the ball rolling, their players wearing red shirts, shorts and socks. Manchester City’s are in their usual home colours.
 Share 1h ago 07.26 EST Not long now: Led by referee Tom Bramall and his team of match officials, both sets of players click-clack out on to the Etihad Stadium pitchon a crisp November afternoon in Manchester. They receive a guard of honour from an array of “Once A Blue” Manchester City legends including Mick McCarthy, Peter Barnes, Paul Lake and Davids White and Brightwell.
 Share 1h ago 07.05 EST Enzo Maresca: The Manchester City boss was asked about the balance – or lack thereof – between attack and defence in his side during his audience with the press yesterday. “The same midfield that won seven games in a row is the same that lost three games in a row,” he said. “It’s football. The idea is to continue to attack in the same way, creating chances, but trying to create a balance when we defend. Sometimes we need more balance and different kind of players on the pitch. We are going to find solutions for a more balanced defensive back line and midfield.
 “I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we were winning games. I’m not thinking we did everything wrong when we lost games. There are things we need to do better and no doubt we will do better. We are conceding too many goals. Most of them are avoidable. So we need to avoid mistakes and try to deal with it [better] when it happens.”
 View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City side come into today’s match on the back of three consecutive defeats. Photograph: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images Share 1h ago 07.04 EST Manchester City: Will Unwin is at the Etihad Stadium for the Guardian and has filed this scene-setter from his place in the press box. “Without going over the top, it feels like a big day for Enzo Maresca,” he says. “After three Premier League defeats in a row, the Italian has to find improvement in his team. To do so, a change in midfield sees Ayyoub Bouaddi brought in to bring additional calmness alongside the all-action Elliot Anderson. With all the uncertainty swirling around this half of Manchester, getting matters on the pitch back on track is imperative. A statement win to prove there is full focus among the squad would be ideal but any will do against Fulham.”
 Share 2h ago 07.02 EST Alvaro Arbeloa: “I have watched all Manchester City games and the last three games that they lost I woudn’t say they were the worst team,” said Fulham’s head coach in yesterday’s press conference. “They have the chances. You can see the quality of the players, how they want to play. They are very, very aggressive when they lose the ball, so for me they are performing really, really well.
 “This is the Premier League , so you can feel how difficult every game is, but they won the first seven games, it was amazing. For me, they’re still one of the best teams in the world.”
 Asked about speculation linking Fulham defender Calvin Bassey with a move to Manchester United, Alvaro stressed the Nigerian international’s importance to the Cottagers. “He’s very, very important,” he said. “He is one of my captains. From the first days when I arrived I saw how good he is. I think he is one of the best centre backs in the world, so it’s normal if there are so many teams that wants Calvin, that for me is normal.
 “I’m not worried about that because I am really happy with Calvin. I think Calvin is really happy here. He is so important for us. He is one of our leaders.”
 View image in fullscreen Alvaro Arbeloa doesn’t think Manchester City are in as much trouble as their recent Premier League results suggest. Photograph: David Horton/CameraSport/Getty Images Share 2h ago 07.01 EST Premier League news: Moyes demands more from Grealish, Iraola wary of United threat Read more Share 2h ago 07.00 EST View image in fullscreen Bernd Leno warms up ahead of kick-off in a match where his Fulham team are hoping to avoid their 21st consecutivbe defeat at the hands of Manchester City. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  07.01 EST 2h ago 06.57 EST Elsewhere in Manchester: Maine Road FC,who play in English football’s tenth tier, aim to become a new home for any Manchester City supporters disillusioned by the possible consequences of the guilty verdict handed down to their team, and those priced out of the Premier League. Dominic Booth reports …
 Maine Road offer non-league haven to fans of scandal-hit Manchester City Read more Share 2h ago 06.55 EST Gonzalo Garica: The Fulham striker and great nephew of Rita Hayworth admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he will remain calm over his 11-match goal drought. Interview: Sid Lowe.
 Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’ Read more View image in fullscreen The Fulham and Spain U-21 striker Gonzalo García says “the intensity and pace” of the Premier League “is very different” to that of La Liga. Photograph: Pablo Garcia/The Guardian Share 2h ago 06.50 EST Today’s match officials
 Referee: Tom Bramall
 Assistants: Gary Beswick and Craig Taylor.
 Fourth official: Sam Barrott.
 VAR: James Bell.
 Assistant VAR: Adam Nunn.
 Share 2h ago 06.50 EST View image in fullscreen A view inside the Etihad Stadium ahead of kick-off. Photograph: Jon Super/Reuters Share 2h ago 06.32 EST Those teams: Enzo Maresca makes three changes to the City team that started against Nottingham Forest last time out, with Nico O’Reilly, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Phil Foden coming into his side. Josko Gvardiol, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki drop to the bench. Abdukodir Khusanov and Marc Guehi have both been selected despite missing out on international duty with Uzbekistan and England resepectively through injury.
 There are also three changes to the Fulham side that lined up against Newcastle before the international break. Kenny Tete, Ryan Sessegnon and Rodrigo Muniz have been selected today, with Timothy Castagne, Antonee Robinson and Gonzalo Garcia making way.
 Share Updated at  06.35 EST 2h ago 06.28 EST Manchester City v Fulham line-ups
 Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly, Anderson, Bouaddi, Ndiaye, Foden, Doku, Haaland
 Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Cherki, Fernandez, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, Samba, Lewis
 Fulham: Leno, Tete, Bassey, Affengruber, Sessegnon, Charles, Berge, Iwobi, King, Bobb, Muniz.
 Subs: Kaiser, Cuenca, García, Palacios, Cairney, Larsson, Angel, Castagne, Robinson.
 Share 2h ago 06.25 EST Early team news
 Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo remains sidelined with the knee injury he suffered against Ipswich in October, while defenders Marc Guehi and Abdukodir Khushanov have been rated doubtful for today’s game.
 Speaking at his press conference yesterday, Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa confirmed that reserve goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will be out for the season after rupturing his achillles tendon in a practice match played against West Ham behind closed doors during the international break.
 Midfielder Tom Cairney is struggling with a knee injury but could feature in today’s squad, while Emile Smith-Rowe is unlikely to be in the matchday squad as he has a hip injury.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo misses out on today’s match as he continues his recovery from a knee injury. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Share 2h ago 06.25 EST Premier League: Manchester City v Fulham
 Following the second international break of the season, the Premier League resumes at the Etihad Stadium, with Manchester City hoping to halt a run of three consecutive defeats in the top flight. The most recent came against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground, where Liam Delap scored two quite extraordinary goals against the club where he learnt his trade.
 Fulham are unbeaten in four matches and came from behind to draw with Newcastle at Craven Cottage last time out. Rather astonishingly, they haven’t beaten Manchester City since 2009 and have lost 20 consecutive games against today’s hosts in an extraordinary run of defeats against the same opponents dating back to 2012. Kick-off at the Etihad Stadium is at 12.30pm (GMT) but we’ll have team news and buildup in the meantime.
